fields.Name: IT99 - Cloudflare Clef Decision Models
fields.Description: Cloudflare's Clef and Clef-flash decision models resolve from the synced metadata through AIDecisionRunner to the Workers AI request, with no network. CF1 Clef and Clef-flash are Active Decision models whose effective Decision limits are 64 questions per call, 255 Choice options, 10 Score levels and 65,536 state tokens; each has one Cloudflare Model Developer row, one Active Cloudflare Inference Provider row naming the CloudflareDecision driver, its @cf/cloudflare APIName and a 65,536-token input limit without streaming, and an active Realtime cost row at $0.24 or $0.09 per million input tokens with free output; the Cloudflare vendor takes an API Key credential. CF2 ClassFactory.CreateInstance(BaseDecision, 'CloudflareDecision', key) returns the shipped CloudflareDecision class, which reads the account ID from a '<accountId>:<apiToken>' key. CF3 a real AIDecisionRunner.ExecuteDecision on the Default Decision prompt, with override naming each model and its Cloudflare vendor and a legacy apiKeys credential, selects that model with CloudflareDecision; the driver POSTs the System One body for a Likelihood, a Choice and a Score question to https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account>/ai/run/<APIName> with the token alone as the bearer and the short model name in the body; the scripted Workers AI response, in Cloudflare's v4 envelope, comes back mapped (Choice probabilities renormalised, Score probabilities keyed by level name); and the MJ: AI Prompt Runs row is recorded against that model and the Cloudflare vendor, successful, with the scripted input tokens and a cost priced from the model's cost row. The network is replaced only at the driver's SendRequest hook, by a subclass registered over CloudflareDecision for the length of CF3 and restored after it. Server transport by necessity: the stand-in is a ClassFactory registration in this process. Every prompt run the bundle creates is deleted in teardown.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Clef and Clef-flash are usable as Decision models: their metadata resolves with the right limits, driver, API names and prices, the driver builds through the ClassFactory, and an AIDecisionRunner call naming either one sends the right Workers AI request, maps its answers and records the run against the model and Cloudflare.
